correctness.rationale: A derivation is D_b(x)=x'b with b in the nilpotent ideal. The pointwise range is either zero or the ideal t^s determined by the least exponent s not divisible by p; this gives a necessary-and-sufficient classification on arbitrary elements. For each eligible column, nested subspaces yield exact rank recursion and maximal-rank product. The residue-class infinite product has strictly positive limit. Exhaustive independent small cases check both direct local condition and rank counts. No numerical experiment is used as infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The complex statement cannot be transported unchanged: every derivation kills t^p, so the corresponding column must vanish. The product formula follows from a new positive-characteristic local-derivation identification plus elementary nested-subspace counting. Prior general matrix bounds do not by themselves supply the local-derivation identification. The possibility that standard Ferrers rank enumeration combined with an undiscovered algebra classification implies this product remains a publication-priority risk.

value.rationale: For canonical nilpotent associative algebras, detects a sharp characteristic-p zero-column obstruction, classifies all local derivations, determines every rank multiplicity, and finds a positive, p-periodic limiting maximal-rank probability, versus the naive triangular n-dimensional full-rank decay. These are structural and asymptotic invariants, rather than arbitrary finite slices.
